messages.subject: inla crash why?
parts:
Dear all,
 
I wonder what was my reason when I run a spde model using inla and it got crashed as below:
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
Calls: inla -> inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed

My model is just the very simple SPDE model with Gaussian family. There are 648,000 data points and 2493 mesh nodes only. The following information when setting verbose=TRUE was pasted in the end. Could anyone please help with this?
 
Kind regards,
Michael

> Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :

> carefully.
>   If this does not help, please contact the developers at <help@r-inl

> a.org>.
> Calls: inla -> inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed
>
> My model is just the very simple SPDE model with Gaussian family.
> There are 648,000 data points and 2493 mesh nodes only. The following
> information when setting verbose=TRUE was pasted in the end. Could
> anyone please help with this?
>

is that the joint precision matrix is numerical singular. In some way, you have to make it more stable.

sometimes you get an INF/NAN error, saying, essentially, that something drifts away to infinity.

You also have a huge dimension (about 600k) of the presicion matrix which makes it more vonarable to such effects.

INLA is not highly efficient in such cases where you have a lot of data and few mesh-points.


I can give it a try if you send me code & data, if you like.
